title: Cells and Living Things Core Test
description: Core practice for living things, cell evidence, and cell structures.

questions.prompt: Which observation is the strongest evidence that a sample is living?
questions.questionText: Which observation is the strongest evidence that a sample is living?
options: It is made of one or more cells.
It has a rough surface.
It changes temperature during the day.
It is found outside in soil.
questions.correctAnswer: It is made of one or more cells.
questions.explanation: Being made of cells is direct evidence of living things. Texture, temperature change, and location do not prove that something is alive.

questions.prompt: A scientist sees a single microscopic structure using energy, growing, and dividing into two similar structures. What conclusion is best supported?
questions.questionText: A scientist sees a single microscopic structure using energy, growing, and dividing into two similar structures. What conclusion is best supported?
options: The structure is likely a living single-celled organism.
The structure must be a nonliving crystal.
The structure cannot be alive because it has only one cell.
The structure is a tissue made of many organs.
questions.correctAnswer: The structure is likely a living single-celled organism.
questions.explanation: Single-celled organisms can be living. The evidence of energy use, growth, and division supports that conclusion.

questions.prompt: Which cell structure controls what enters and leaves the cell?
questions.questionText: Which cell structure controls what enters and leaves the cell?
options: cell membrane
chloroplast
nucleus
mitochondrion
questions.correctAnswer: cell membrane
questions.explanation: The cell membrane forms a boundary and controls movement into and out of the cell.

questions.prompt: A plant cell has a stiff outer layer that helps it keep its shape. Which structure is being described?
questions.questionText: A plant cell has a stiff outer layer that helps it keep its shape. Which structure is being described?
options: cell wall
cell membrane
nucleus
mitochondrion
questions.correctAnswer: cell wall
questions.explanation: The cell wall gives plant cells extra support and helps maintain shape.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the relationship between a cell part and the whole cell?
questions.questionText: Which statement best describes the relationship between a cell part and the whole cell?
options: Cell parts have jobs that help the cell function as a system.
Each cell part can survive forever without the rest of the cell.
Only one cell part does all jobs for the cell.
Cell parts are unrelated to the needs of the cell.
questions.correctAnswer: Cell parts have jobs that help the cell function as a system.
questions.explanation: A cell is a system because its parts interact and contribute to the function of the whole cell.

questions.prompt: Which structure is most directly involved in using light energy to make sugars in many plant cells?
questions.questionText: Which structure is most directly involved in using light energy to make sugars in many plant cells?
options: chloroplast
cell wall
nucleus
cell membrane
questions.correctAnswer: chloroplast
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts capture light energy and help make sugars during photosynthesis.

questions.prompt: A student claims that animal cells and plant cells are identical because both are living cells. Which evidence best challenges the claim?
questions.questionText: A student claims that animal cells and plant cells are identical because both are living cells. Which evidence best challenges the claim?
options: Plant cells usually have cell walls and chloroplasts, while animal cells do not.
Both plant and animal cells have cell membranes.
Both plant and animal cells use energy.
Animal cells and plant cells can both be seen with microscopes.
questions.correctAnswer: Plant cells usually have cell walls and chloroplasts, while animal cells do not.
questions.explanation: The claim says the cells are identical. Evidence about cell walls and chloroplasts shows an important difference.

questions.prompt: Which example best shows structure and function in a cell?
questions.questionText: Which example best shows structure and function in a cell?
options: The flexible membrane surrounds the cell and helps control movement of materials.
A cell is too small to see without a microscope.
A living thing may contain many cells.
Cells were first studied by scientists using lenses.
questions.correctAnswer: The flexible membrane surrounds the cell and helps control movement of materials.
questions.explanation: This connects the membrane's structure as a boundary with its function controlling what enters and leaves.

questions.prompt: A sample grows larger because more mineral crystals attach to it. It has no cells and does not use energy. Which conclusion is best?
questions.questionText: A sample grows larger because more mineral crystals attach to it. It has no cells and does not use energy. Which conclusion is best?
options: The sample is probably nonliving, even though it gets larger.
The sample is living because all growth proves life.
The sample is living because minerals are cells.
The sample must be a multicellular organism.
questions.correctAnswer: The sample is probably nonliving, even though it gets larger.
questions.explanation: Growth alone is not enough evidence for life. The lack of cells and energy use supports the conclusion that the sample is nonliving.

questions.prompt: Which sequence correctly shows increasing organization in a multicellular organism?
questions.questionText: Which sequence correctly shows increasing organization in a multicellular organism?
options: cell, tissue, organ, organ system
organ system, organ, tissue, cell
tissue, cell, organ system, organ
cell wall, organ, tissue, organism
questions.correctAnswer: cell, tissue, organ, organ system
questions.explanation: Cells form tissues, tissues form organs, and organs work together in organ systems.

questions.prompt: A microscope view shows many box-like plant cells. Most boxes have a dark round structure near the center. Which structure is the dark round part most likely showing?
questions.questionText: A microscope view shows many box-like plant cells. Most boxes have a dark round structure near the center. Which structure is the dark round part most likely showing?
options: nucleus
cell wall
chloroplast
cell membrane
questions.correctAnswer: nucleus
questions.explanation: The nucleus is often drawn or seen as a darker structure inside the cell because it contains genetic information.

questions.prompt: A student compares a classroom to a cell. The classroom door controls what enters and leaves. Which cell structure has the most similar job?
questions.questionText: A student compares a classroom to a cell. The classroom door controls what enters and leaves. Which cell structure has the most similar job?
options: cell membrane
mitochondrion
chloroplast
vacuole
questions.correctAnswer: cell membrane
questions.explanation: The membrane controls movement of materials into and out of a cell, like a door controls movement into and out of a room.

questions.prompt: Which evidence would best support the claim that a pond sample contains living organisms?
questions.questionText: Which evidence would best support the claim that a pond sample contains living organisms?
options: The sample contains microscopic cells with visible boundaries.
The sample is green.
The sample came from outdoors.
The sample has small pieces of sand.
questions.correctAnswer: The sample contains microscopic cells with visible boundaries.
questions.explanation: Cells are direct evidence for living things. Color and location alone are weaker evidence.

questions.prompt: A single-celled organism takes in food particles through its boundary. Which structure must be working to control what crosses that boundary?
questions.questionText: A single-celled organism takes in food particles through its boundary. Which structure must be working to control what crosses that boundary?
options: cell membrane
cell wall
nucleus
chloroplast
questions.correctAnswer: cell membrane
questions.explanation: The cell membrane controls movement across the cell boundary.

questions.prompt: Which model best represents a multicellular organism as a system?
questions.questionText: Which model best represents a multicellular organism as a system?
options: many specialized cells forming tissues, organs, and organ systems
one cell part doing every job alone
minerals attaching to a rock surface
a single organ floating without cells
questions.correctAnswer: many specialized cells forming tissues, organs, and organ systems
questions.explanation: Multicellular organisms are organized systems built from specialized cells.

questions.prompt: A student says, "All cells have chloroplasts because all cells need energy." Which evidence best corrects the idea?
questions.questionText: A student says, "All cells have chloroplasts because all cells need energy." Which evidence best corrects the idea?
options: Animal cells use energy but usually do not have chloroplasts.
Plant cells are usually larger than atoms.
Cells can be seen with microscopes.
Some cells have membranes.
questions.correctAnswer: Animal cells use energy but usually do not have chloroplasts.
questions.explanation: Many cells use energy without chloroplasts. Chloroplasts are common in plant cells that make sugars using light.

questions.prompt: A table lists two samples: Sample A has cells and uses energy. Sample B has no cells and does not use energy. Which claim is best supported?
questions.questionText: A table lists two samples: Sample A has cells and uses energy. Sample B has no cells and does not use energy. Which claim is best supported?
options: Sample A is more likely living than Sample B.
Sample B is more likely living because it has fewer parts.
Both samples must be plants.
Neither sample can be studied with evidence.
questions.correctAnswer: Sample A is more likely living than Sample B.
questions.explanation: The data show stronger life evidence for Sample A because cells and energy use are features of living things.

questions.prompt: Which structure-function match is accurate?
questions.questionText: Which structure-function match is accurate?
options: mitochondrion: helps release usable energy from food molecules
nucleus: makes the stiff outer wall of plants
cell membrane: stores all genetic instructions in chromosomes
chloroplast: controls every material entering animal cells
questions.correctAnswer: mitochondrion: helps release usable energy from food molecules
questions.explanation: Mitochondria help cells release usable energy from food molecules.

questions.prompt: A plant wilts when its cells lose water. Which cell structure helps plant cells stay rigid when water is available?
questions.questionText: A plant wilts when its cells lose water. Which cell structure helps plant cells stay rigid when water is available?
options: cell wall
nucleus
mitochondrion
cell membrane only
questions.correctAnswer: cell wall
questions.explanation: The cell wall gives plant cells support and helps them keep shape.

questions.prompt: A student claims, "A microscope is useful only for nonliving things." Which evidence best challenges the claim?
questions.questionText: A student claims, "A microscope is useful only for nonliving things." Which evidence best challenges the claim?
options: Microscopes can reveal cells in onion skin and cheek samples.
Microscopes are made of glass and metal.
Some rocks are shiny under light.
A microscope can sit on a table.
questions.correctAnswer: Microscopes can reveal cells in onion skin and cheek samples.
questions.explanation: Cells in living samples are often too small to see without a microscope.

questions.prompt: A diagram labels a cell wall outside a cell membrane. Which statement best interprets the model?
questions.questionText: A diagram labels a cell wall outside a cell membrane. Which statement best interprets the model?
options: A plant cell can have both a supportive wall and a selective membrane.
The wall replaces the need for a membrane.
Only animal cells have cell walls.
The membrane is outside the wall in all cells.
questions.correctAnswer: A plant cell can have both a supportive wall and a selective membrane.
questions.explanation: Plant cells commonly have a cell wall outside the membrane; the two structures have different jobs.

questions.prompt: A scientist finds an unknown organism made of one cell with no chloroplasts. Which conclusion is most reasonable?
questions.questionText: A scientist finds an unknown organism made of one cell with no chloroplasts. Which conclusion is most reasonable?
options: It may still be living because not all living cells have chloroplasts.
It cannot be living because every cell needs chloroplasts.
It must be a plant leaf cell.
It is an organ system.
questions.correctAnswer: It may still be living because not all living cells have chloroplasts.
questions.explanation: Some living cells, including many single-celled organisms and animal cells, do not have chloroplasts.

questions.prompt: Which investigation would best test whether a mystery sample is made of cells?
questions.questionText: Which investigation would best test whether a mystery sample is made of cells?
options: Prepare a slide and observe the sample under a microscope.
Measure the color of the container.
Ask whether the sample came from a garden.
Shake the sample and listen for sound.
questions.correctAnswer: Prepare a slide and observe the sample under a microscope.
questions.explanation: Direct observation with a microscope can provide evidence for cells.

questions.prompt: A model shows nucleus -> instructions, chloroplast -> sugar-making, mitochondrion -> energy release, membrane -> controlled boundary. What does the model emphasize?
questions.questionText: A model shows nucleus -> instructions, chloroplast -> sugar-making, mitochondrion -> energy release, membrane -> controlled boundary. What does the model emphasize?
options: Cell parts have different jobs that support the whole cell.
Every cell part has exactly the same function.
Cells do not need materials from the environment.
Only one part of a cell is living.
questions.correctAnswer: Cell parts have different jobs that support the whole cell.
questions.explanation: The model connects several structures to functions that help the cell work as a system.

questions.prompt: A student argues that a chicken egg from a grocery store is a complete multicellular organism because it is large. What is the best scientific response?
questions.questionText: A student argues that a chicken egg from a grocery store is a complete multicellular organism because it is large. What is the best scientific response?
options: Size alone is not enough; evidence such as cells, organization, and life processes matters.
Anything large must be a full organism.
Only small things can be living.
Cells are not relevant to living things.
questions.correctAnswer: Size alone is not enough; evidence such as cells, organization, and life processes matters.
questions.explanation: Large size does not prove something is a complete living organism. Scientific claims need relevant evidence.

questions.prompt: Which observation best links cell structure to survival?
questions.questionText: Which observation best links cell structure to survival?
options: A membrane lets needed materials enter while helping keep harmful materials out.
A cell is always square.
A cell wall makes all organisms move faster.
A nucleus is found outside the cell.
questions.correctAnswer: A membrane lets needed materials enter while helping keep harmful materials out.
questions.explanation: Selective movement across the membrane helps a cell maintain conditions needed for life.

questions.prompt: A tissue sample contracts when stimulated. What is the best connection to cells?
questions.questionText: A tissue sample contracts when stimulated. What is the best connection to cells?
options: The tissue contains specialized cells whose structures support contraction.
The tissue cannot be living because tissues do not contain cells.
Only the whole organ can have specialized cells.
Contraction proves it is made of minerals.
questions.correctAnswer: The tissue contains specialized cells whose structures support contraction.
questions.explanation: Tissues are groups of specialized cells working together.

questions.prompt: Which question would best deepen a model of how a cell works as a system?
questions.questionText: Which question would best deepen a model of how a cell works as a system?
options: How do the cell parts interact to meet the cell's needs?
What is the prettiest color in the diagram?
Can the diagram be drawn larger?
What is the name of the classroom?
questions.correctAnswer: How do the cell parts interact to meet the cell's needs?
questions.explanation: A system model should show relationships and interactions, not only labels.

questions.prompt: A student sees a cell with a cell wall, chloroplasts, a nucleus, and a membrane. Which claim is best supported?
questions.questionText: A student sees a cell with a cell wall, chloroplasts, a nucleus, and a membrane. Which claim is best supported?
options: The cell is most likely from a plant or plant-like organism.
The cell must be an animal muscle cell.
The cell has no structures with functions.
The cell cannot use energy.
questions.correctAnswer: The cell is most likely from a plant or plant-like organism.
questions.explanation: Cell walls and chloroplasts are strong evidence for plant or plant-like cells.

questions.prompt: Which explanation best connects cells to the larger organism?
questions.questionText: Which explanation best connects cells to the larger organism?
options: Cells carry out jobs; groups of specialized cells form structures that help the organism function.
Cells are unrelated to tissues and organs.
Organs make cells unnecessary.
A living thing is living only if it has one cell.
questions.correctAnswer: Cells carry out jobs; groups of specialized cells form structures that help the organism function.
questions.explanation: This connects cell function to tissues, organs, organ systems, and the whole organism.
